basis: Intellectual disability and distal skeletal defects define the syndrome; developmental delay occurs in 16/16 and peripheral neurologic abnormalities are common.
Benign adipose tumours most commonly arise in subcutaneous tissue; deep muscular or visceral locations do not characterize most patients.
Defective skin appendages and dental development characterize the group; neurologic, immune and ocular disease are subtype-specific.
Inherited podocyte disease causing steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, mesangial sclerosis and kidney failure in 2/2.
Deficient aldosterone production defines this endocrine disorder; salt wasting does not establish intrinsic kidney damage.
Malignant tumour arising in the urinary bladder neck.
Intellectual disability, congenital contractures and distal amyotrophy define the disease; oculomotor apraxia is neurologic rather than intrinsic eye damage.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with developmental impairment and skeletal defects; cataracts in 2/2. Chronic lung disease in 1/2 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Limb shortening and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; gingival overgrowth, bifid tongue and dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Immune-mediated oral ulceration and auricular chondritis define MAGIC; keratitis/scleritis occur in 30-79%. Nasal chondritis, also 30-79%, omitted under cap.
Retinal response recovery is impaired, causing persistent difficulty adapting to luminance changes and visual impairment.
Mutilating keratoderma defines the disease; persistent lip inflammation occurs in 4/4 and fixed digital flexion contracture in 1/1 assessed patient.
Developmental disability and skeletal overgrowth/maturation abnormalities characterize the syndrome; cataract and myopia reported in 1/1 assessed patient.
Severe developmental impairment, hydronephrosis and skeletal anomalies define SGS; cardiac malformations occur in 30-79%. Visual impairment, 30-79%, omitted under cap.
Structural skeletal myopathy; cardiomegaly and heart failure in 1/2. Respiratory weakness does not establish intrinsic pulmonary disease.
Cowden phenotype includes characteristic mucocutaneous lesions and gastrointestinal hamartomas; cancer susceptibility alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; optic disc pallor indicates optic nerve damage in 4/11 (~36%). Retinal dystrophy alone is below threshold at 2/12.
Cerebral motor dysfunction causes ataxia and spastic diplegia; spasticity alone does not establish intrinsic muscle or joint disease.
Bent-bone dysplasia defines the disease; intellectual disability is annotated in 30-79%. Dental, thyroid and haematologic findings are only occasional.
Motor-neuron degeneration, sometimes with frontotemporal dementia; muscle wasting and ventilatory weakness reflect denervation.
Inherited reductase deficiency disrupts haemoglobin redox metabolism. Neurologic damage belongs mainly to minority generalized type II; the 1/1 HPO sample is not representative.
Combined immune dysfunction with deficient immunoglobulins defines SCID; recurrent thrush and other infections are separately diagnosed consequences.
Extensive myelomeningocele involves spinal cord and meninges herniating through vertebral arch defects.
Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts causes cholestatic liver injury; associated autoimmune diseases do not add organ labels.
Fibrosis and sclerosis are located in the tympanic membrane and middle ear; hearing loss is not required.
